## Suggested starting points

| Project scope | Suggested projects |
|---|---|
| BSc with lower setup risk | 1.1 C-MAPSS, 1.4 MovieLens, 2.2 UCI-HAR, 3.1 EuroSAT RGB |
| MSc with a defined method extension | 1.2 dynamic traffic graph, 2.4 decomposition-aware forecasting, 3.1 vision adapter, 4.1 deep-unfolded multivariate VMD |
| MSc with higher methodological risk | 2.1 Tetra Pak regime-aware SSL, 2.3 lead-aware latent prediction, 2.6 physics-grounded vibration graphs, 4.1 coupled deep-unfolded VMD |
| Preliminary checks required | 2.1 Tetra Pak after the partner-data profile and agreement; 2.5 HEAPO after a licence and data check; 4.1 LargeST licence and applied-data check |

## A simple decision process

1. Choose the **task**, not the fashionable model: node classification, link prediction, graph prediction, temporal forecasting or representation learning.
2. Download the data and run one complete baseline on a small subset before the formal project begins.
3. Write a one-sentence research question and identify the comparison that could falsify the proposed explanation.
4. Freeze the split, primary metric and compute budget before extensive development.
5. Treat the authors' repository as an executable specification—not as the thesis contribution.

## Week-one feasibility checklist

- Obtain access to the exact dataset and record its version, size, licence or data agreement, and release date or extraction period.
- Run the simplest baseline from raw input to final metric on a small subset.
- Identify the independent split unit and verify that it cannot cross train and test.
- Record the anchor paper, repository version and preprocessing deviations.
- Estimate training time and peak memory before planning seeds or ablations.
- For MSc work, write the question, proposed mechanism, main alternative explanation and minimum viable ablation table.

## Licences and access

| Resource | Licence or status | Practical consequence |
|---|---|---|
| UCI-HAR | CC BY 4.0 | Open with attribution |
| PTB-XL | CC BY 4.0 | No credentialing required |
| Paderborn KAt | CC BY-NC 4.0 | Non-commercial academic use |
| MVTec AD | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | Non-commercial and share-alike |
| DINOv2 | Apache 2.0 | Ungated |
| DINOv3 weights | Custom Meta licence | Gated; non-standard; review for industry use |
| HEAPO data | No dataset licence displayed in Zenodo Rights metadata | Confirm before starting; code and paper have separate licences |
| Tetra Pak process data | Partner-supplied under an approved agreement | Restricted access; confirm scope and secure environment before allocation |

## Recurring failure modes

- Comparing with a number produced by a different split, metric, horizon, shot count or evaluation level.
- Using windows from the same physical unit in both training and test sets.
- Calling an authors' repository run a research contribution.
- Reporting only in-distribution performance when transfer or cold start is the motivation.
- Omitting the random frozen encoder in a self-supervised study.
- Treating a recent preprint figure as a settled benchmark.
- Expanding to a second dataset before the first pipeline and evaluation protocol are stable.

Select one primary question, fix the evaluation protocol before extensive experimentation and report negative as well as positive results.

The Tetra Pak project is included as Project 2.1. A Siemens Gamesa project may be offered separately when its scope and data access are confirmed.
